thread:
alice (infra): FYI we're seeing a weird partial failover to eu-west due to DNS split-horizon + long TTLs. Some regions still hitting the degraded us-central GPU fleet :rotating_light:

bob (sre): Seeing high retry rates and token queueing on us-central gpus, pods not draining. Is DNS still pointing at old endpoints?

charlie (netops): Confirmed — authoritative records were updated 30m ago but TTLs were 600. A subset of resolvers still returning old A records. Also noticed that our Cloud DNS health-checks showed intermittent 502s which delayed failover automation.

alice (infra): Ouch. We reduced app LB weights but because of cached DNS clients, traffic kept trickling to the failing region and aclogger shows higher p99 latency. Need urgent TTL downshift + cache flush guidance.

bob (sre): Plan: 1) Lower DNS TTL to 30s on the zone (Cloudflare) 2) Trigger CDN/edge cache purge 3) Push explicit fallback IPs via traffic-manager as emergency 4) Coordinate with infra team to decrement weight on us-central further.

charlie (netops): I'm on DNS change. Updating SOA and all records to TTL=30 via `cli dns update --zone=redwood.ai --record='*' --ttl=30` then `cfapi purge` for the CDN. Will post API calls.

alice (infra): While TTL propagates, we should send a targeted BGP withdraw for the us-central edge IP block to accelerate convergence. Can netops do a withdraw for the edge-anycast prefix?

charlie (netops): I can request an emergency withdraw with peering ops. Doing it now. Note: withdraw will cause brief packet loss for some low-latency clients but it's faster than waiting for caches.

dana (oncall): I'm watching the autoscaler. There's stuck pods in Drain state for the gpus cluster — kubelet shows `eviction threshold` warnings. I've restarted the node-controller to force re-evaluation.

bob (sre): Good. Also toggled fallback model routing for high-priority traffic so it goes to dedicated fallbacks (quantized models) rather than queuing on degraded GPUs. That reduces tail latency for critical requests.

deploy-bot: alert: route-adjustment applied by bob (sre) — fallback-policy=v1-quant; started 1860123572

alice (infra): For verification run `dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai` and `curl -I https://api.redwood.ai/health` from multiple regions. Post outputs here.

charlie (netops): dig from our peering box (ams): `api.redwood.ai -> 52.17.23.45` (new), from colo in us-east: `52.17.23.45`, from legacy resolver in partner infra: `35.169.11.8` (old). So still split-horizon at partner resolver.

dana (oncall): Partner resolver is known to ignore TTLs >300 unless explicitly flushed. Pinged partner ops (ticket #PL-4521) to request a cache flush. They've acknowledged.

bob (sre): In parallel, I'm patching the node draining playbook to forcibly cordon and `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0` for stuck inference pods if they block autoscaler. Will only run on targeted nodes.

alice (infra): Communication note: update status page and incident channel (postmortem link placeholder). Also prepare to revert TTL to standard (5m) after stable.

charlie (netops): BGP withdraw executed for prefix 203.0.113.0/24, announced failover to alternate anycast. Waiting 60s for global RIB convergence.

dana (oncall): After withdraw, curl health from the same partner resolver endpoint now returns 200 and traces show traffic landing in eu-west fallback nodes. Latency improved on tail.

bob (sre): kube drain forced on 2 nodes, pods rescheduled successfully to eu-west. GPU queue depth dropped ~70%.

alice (infra): OK — once partner confirms full cache flush and we see stable endpoints from their resolver, we'll escalate TTL back up to 300 and re-announce BGP for normal topology. Tagging this for post-incident: TTL baseline too high for emergency role, add playbook step to proactively set short TTLs during maintenance windows.

charlie (netops): Partner confirmed cache flush at 1860123680. I restored normal DNS TTL to 300 and re-announced original BGP for the prefix at 1860123705.

deploy-bot: incident: status=mitigated; summary="Partial DNS cache retention + long TTL caused slow failover, BGP withdraw + DNS TTL downshift + forced pod drain mitigated"; incident_id=INC-2026-0421

dana (oncall): Will start a concise postmortem draft. Action items: TTL emergency mode, partner resolver runbook, auto-drain safeguards for kube autoscaler, add probe to detect split-horizon via multi-resolver dig checks.

alice (infra): Thanks everyone. Leaving this thread open till postmortem doc is linked. :thumbsup:
